## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Āyatanavibhaṅga* is the second chapter of the *Vibhaṅga*, which forms the second treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [Hazra 1994; SuttaCentral]. It provides an analytical Abhidhamma exposition of the sense bases (*āyatana*), corresponding in doctrinal theme to the *Saḷāyatanavibhaṅga Sutta* (MN 137) of the Sutta Piṭaka [Hazra 1994]. SuttaCentral records one modern translation of the text and lists a passage-level canonical parallel in the *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23) [SuttaCentral].
Text-reuse computations indicate that the *Āyatanavibhaṅga* shares dense textual material with other Abhidhamma treatises [DharmaNexus]. Within the Pali canon, its largest internal overlaps occur with companion chapters of the *Vibhaṅga*—chiefly the *Khandhavibhaṅga* (Vb 1), *Dhātuvibhaṅga* (Vb 3), *Indriyavibhaṅga* (Vb 5), and *Saccavibhaṅga* (Vb 4)—as well as sections of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi* (notably the *Rūpavibhatti*, Ds 2.2.3) and the *Paṭṭhāna* [DharmaNexus]. Externally, DharmaNexus identifies textual alignments with Sanskrit, Tibetan, and Chinese scholastic works analyzing the sense bases and mental factors, including Nāgārjuna's *Dharmasaṃgraha*, Vasubandhu's *Pañcaskandhaprakaraṇa*, Sthiramati's *Pañcaskandhakavibhāṣā*, Ghoṣaka's *Abhidharmāmṛta*, the *Yogācārabhūmi*, and the Tibetan translation of the *Abhidharmakośabhāṣya* [DharmaNexus].
